subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this cross-product localization contract, including recipient locale ownership, Gateway metadata, plugin metadata, and release-blocking completeness gates?
rationale: The RFC establishes durable APIs and operational obligations across core, channels, plugins, clients, and release management; repository policy requires explicit maintainer acceptance for that direction.

options.title: Continue and revise
options.body: Keep the RFC draft, align it with the existing command localization API, and resolve each owner decision before acceptance.

options.title: Narrow the first RFC
options.body: Standardize only locale resolution and runtime message descriptors, deferring metadata and release gates to later RFCs.

options.title: Decline the shared contract
options.body: Keep localization surface-owned and avoid a cross-product runtime and completeness program.

recommendation.title: Continue and revise
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC draft, align it with the existing command localization API, and resolve each owner decision before acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the clearest prior product-direction signal on coordinated localization architecture.
